ensemble.selection: World, meta_Ch3vetted_withclimate categories C1 and C3. Require total, coal, oil, gas, biomass, nuclear, solar, wind for every decade 2020–2100; positive totals and nonnegative values. Reject component sums above total by more than 0.01%. Four non-closing IMAGE scenarios are excluded. No restriction based on the resulting technology shares.
ensemble.interpretation: Unweighted scenario percentiles in the selected literature sample, not probabilities, model-balanced consensus or a single feasible mix. Model/scenario representation is uneven; source-wise medians need not sum to 100%.
ensemble.licence: IIASA/IAMC AR6 database terms permit educational/scientific communication with attribution; database rights retained. Small numerical subset only, not the full database.

solar.approximation: 2025 is nearly 2700 TWh, about 600 TWh above 2024; both generation values rounded.
solar.guide_assumptions: Constant 2025 IRENA net PV addition rate; full-year output from each additional GW; no retirements through 2035. Demand anchored at IEA 2025 then follows relative AR6 C1/C3 ensemble median total-energy change. Illustrative guide, not an integrated model update.

fusion_mit.extraction: Vector line vertices from Fig.4.4b; axes x=195.71–466.93 pt maps 2020–2100, y=545.36–392.02 pt maps 0–50000 TWh. Rounded to nearest 100 TWh; the base-case 2035=2 TWh and 2050=375 TWh are replaced by exact text values on p.42. Values below ~100 TWh are unresolved in the other cost curves, not proof of zero production.
fusion_mit.costs: Four US overnight-capital costs in 2050: 2800, 5600, 8000, 11300 USD2021/kW; further cost reduction thereafter. Base case 8000 in 2050, ~4300 in 2100.
fusion_mit.assumptions: Accelerated climate action; commercial availability in 2035 is assumed, not predicted. Variable-renewable integration costs/resource constraints and regional fission constraints influence the result.
fusion_mit.scaling: Electricity output converted to EJ, divided by the same year’s AR6 ensemble median total primary energy. Cross-model scaling, not an integrated AR6 run.

fusion_etm_timeline.case: S02: early availability, fast diffusion, restricted VRE, reference cost
fusion_etm_timeline.extraction: Approximate yellow fusion segments of Global electricity mix (S2) bars. Embedded image 622×356 px, baseline y=333, 140000 TWh grid at y=13. Centres x=125,243,360,480; segment heights read including antialiasing and rounded to 500 TWh. Linear connections show dated samples only, not additional model outputs.
fusion_etm_timeline.assumptions: SSP2/RCP2.6 root; early fusion availability 2035, fast diffusion tied to tritium availability, restriction on variable renewables. Poster states fusion costs are desired targets, not estimates. S02 reaches 22% of electricity in 2100; S23 late/slow/unrestricted VRE yields much less.
fusion_etm_timeline.scaling: Electricity output converted to EJ, divided by the same year’s AR6 ensemble median total primary energy. Cross-model scaling, not an integrated AR6 run.

fusion.interpretation: Approximate 2100 cross-model scaling against the AR6 ensemble median primary demand, not a combined model or published primary-energy share
requirements: rapid capacity growth comparable to 1970s fission

notes: IPCC AR6 C1/C3 literature ranges, not probabilities or a forecast. Source-wise medians are not a coherent energy mix. Fusion cases are published electricity outputs scaled to the AR6 median total with direct-equivalent accounting, not integrated model results.
source: IEA Global Energy Review 2026 p.44; IPCC AR6 Scenarios Database v1.1, vetted C1/C3; MIT fusion report 2024 Fig.4.4b; Mantilla et al. ESSRI 2024 S02 and 2026 doi:10.1016/j.esr.2026.102326.
